A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STACO research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original linear- and deep-model experiments, benchmark scores, training curves, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds surrogate-loss comparisons and per-iteration runtime measurements in Tables 3 and 4.

M1.justification: The STACO1/STACO2 objectives, block-coordinate updates, and proximal procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–4. The new loss study evaluates surrogate choices without introducing a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use HIGGS, SUSY, ijcnn1, molmuv target 1, moltox21 target 0, nodulemnist3d, and adrenalmnist3d. The dataset statistics match exactly; the added experiments retain this coverage.

E2.justification: The new efficiency comparison in Table 4 includes PAUCI alongside SOTA and SONX, whereas v1's time-based deep-training comparisons included only SOTA and SONX. The baseline membership in the main accuracy table is unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments vary the surrogate among squared hinge, square, and hinge losses and measure runtime in seconds per iteration. The existing splits, architectures, TPAUC regions, training budgets, and tuning settings in Section 5.1 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds a surrogate-loss sensitivity study on the three linear-model datasets, reported in Table 3. The negative-batch-size and epoch-decay ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state five-fold cross-validation and report means and standard deviations over multiple runs. The new loss table follows this practice; no new seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are specified.

E6.justification: Table 2's numerical entries and all original plot images are unchanged. Tables 3 and 4 add loss-dependent scores and runtimes; for example, molmuv runtime is reported as 8.72 seconds per iteration for STACO versus 9.78 for SONX.

T1.justification: v2 adds filtration definitions and an explicit derivation of the D2 bound in Appendix C.2.1, Eqs. 36–40, replacing reliance on a cited bound. This expansion contains sign/index inconsistencies. The theorem statements and rates remain unchanged, while existing Moreau-envelope material moves into Section 4.3.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about STACO, improved convergence, and generalization. The introduction makes mini-batch speedup more explicit, but that contribution was already claimed and quantified in v1.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly attributes abrupt training-performance drops to excessive step sizes. Appendix B.1 acknowledges the Figure 5c instability exception and sensitivity to tuning two learning rates. v2 also interprets the new loss-sensitivity and runtime results.

D1.justification: Table 4 newly documents per-iteration training times. Existing implementation and hyperparameter disclosures are unchanged, and v2 supplies no corresponding hardware or detailed timing procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning against Li et al.'s Smoothed PLDA and citations to Ogryczak and Tamir and Juditsky et al. It also corrects SONX's characterization from inapplicable to convex settings to retaining its slower complexity there. Publication updates to existing references are not new research additions.

P1.justification: The introduction and proof explanations receive targeted revisions, including CVaR explanation and proof-step guidance. Moreau-envelope background and the regularized reformulation exchange main-text/appendix placement. Author information and acknowledgments change, while the overall section structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different journal layout throughout, with a redesigned title/author block, running headers, changed typography and text width, and enlarged/repositioned displays. Tables 3 and 4 are added; the dataset table becomes Table 5. All six original figures retain their plot content.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful loss-sensitivity and runtime evidence and more candid instability caveats. However, the newly expanded proof introduces a sign inconsistency in Eq. 36 and cancelling identical terms in Eq. 38, leaving its mathematical justification problematic. These empirical and explanatory gains coexist with new proof defects, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
